questions.question: State the distance, midpoint and gradient formulae, and apply all three to A(−1; 3) and B(5; 11), showing your working.
questions.expected_answer: Distance: the square root of (x₂ − x₁)² + (y₂ − y₁)². Midpoint: ((x₁ + x₂)/2 ; (y₁ + y₂)/2). Gradient: (y₂ − y₁)/(x₂ − x₁). For A(−1; 3) and B(5; 11): the change in x is 5 − (−1) = 6 and the change in y is 11 − 3 = 8. Distance AB = √(6² + 8²) = √(36 + 64) = √100 = 10 units. Midpoint = ((−1 + 5)/2 ; (3 + 11)/2) = (2; 7). Gradient = 8/6 = 4/3, meaning the line climbs 4 units for every 3 units across. Remember that the midpoint formula is the only one of the three that adds the coordinates; distance and gradient both subtract.

questions.question: Describe the four possible cases for the gradient of a line, and state the conditions for parallel lines and for perpendicular lines, including the pair of lines for which the perpendicular test cannot be used.
questions.expected_answer: A positive gradient rises from left to right; a negative gradient falls from left to right; a gradient of zero means a horizontal line, because the change in y is zero; and a vertical line has an undefined gradient, because the change in x is zero and division by zero has no meaning — undefined is not the same as zero. Parallel lines have equal gradients. Perpendicular lines have gradients whose product is −1, equivalently one gradient is the negative reciprocal of the other: 4/3 pairs with −3/4, and 4/3 × (−3/4) = −1. The product test cannot be used for a horizontal line paired with a vertical line: they are perpendicular, but their gradients are zero and undefined, so no product exists and the case is stated by inspection.

questions.question: For A(−1; 3), B(5; 11), C(10; 8) and D(4; 0), prove that ABCD is a parallelogram and explain why it is neither a rectangle nor a rhombus.
questions.expected_answer: Side lengths: AB = √(6² + 8²) = 10 and CD = √((−6)² + (−8)²) = 10; BC = √(5² + (−3)²) = √34 and DA = √((−5)² + 3²) = √34. Both pairs of opposite sides are equal, a condition for a parallelogram. Gradients confirm it: gradient AB = 8/6 = 4/3 and gradient DC = 8/6 = 4/3, so AB ∥ DC; gradient AD = −3/5 and gradient BC = −3/5, so AD ∥ BC. A third proof: the midpoint of AC is (4,5; 5,5) and the midpoint of BD is (4,5; 5,5), so the diagonals bisect each other. It is not a rectangle because gradient AB × gradient AD = 4/3 × (−3/5) = −4/5, which is not −1, so angle A is not a right angle. It is not a rhombus because 10 does not equal √34, so the four sides are not all equal. ABCD is therefore a parallelogram and nothing more.
